svg.text: Fusion: how many noisy depth views become one surface (TSDF, 1.5mm voxels, ±6mm band)
1. Each view measures the wall, with noise
cross-section through the object's wall
inside the object
Dots: each view's depth readings (±1-2mm noise).
Red crosses: flying pixels at the silhouette, dropped first.
2. One view writes into a band of voxels
along each ray, around the surface that view measured
±6mm truncation band
1 voxel = 1.5mm
free space: clamped at +1
in front of the reading: +
behind the reading: −
over 6mm behind: not updated
3. Average all views; surface = where it's 0
weighted average of signed distances per voxel
seen by 1 view only: not kept in observed.obj
Dashed: three views' readings. Solid: fused surface,
kept where at least 2 views wrote (weight ≥ 2).
WHAT GETS THROWN OUT, AND WHERE
Per view, before fusion
5 frames at each stop: per-pixel median; a pixel valid in fewer than half the frames is dropped.
Pixels next to a depth jump (more than 5mm or 2%) are dropped: flying pixels at silhouettes.
Points outside the object's box + 12mm, or less than 2.5mm above that view's own table fit.
During fusion
Each reading only updates voxels within ±6mm of it along its ray; farther behind is left alone
(another view may see that region). Readings are averaged, never thrown out, so noise cancels.
When the surface is extracted
Only where at least 2 views wrote (one view, alone, keeps all it saw).
Fragments under 5% of the largest piece are removed; light smoothing (5 Taubin steps).
